title: Use the tickets with a deadline
hook: Six tickets expire after this event. Which choice leaves fewer of them unused?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Choose among equivalent resources using a stated expiration deadline.

misconception: Equivalent resources have identical consequences regardless of deadline.
objective: Choose among equivalent resources using a stated expiration deadline.

claims.text: Six tickets expire at the event’s end. Six others remain valid later. Use four before the deadline. Scaled model; fictional tickets; equal acceptance; no food guidance.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Used=4, A=2tickets and B=6tickets. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-",6,"x"]]; B=6; x denotes Used. At x=4, A=2, B=6; recall at x=6: B=6. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Using deadline tickets first reduces the expiring remainder. Using the other tickets leaves all six deadline tickets unused. This is a declared ticket-validity model, not guidance about food or unsafe expired goods.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-",6,"x"]]; B=6; x denotes Used. At x=4, A=2, B=6; recall at x=6: B=6. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: Six tickets expire at the event’s end. Six others remain valid later. Use four before the deadline. Change only Used to 6. What is B (Other-first) now? Correct: 6tickets. Use B's stated rule with Used=6: it gives 6tickets. Using deadline tickets first reduces the expiring remainder. Using the other tickets leaves all six deadline tickets unused. This is a declared ticket-validity model, not guidance about food or unsafe expired goods.

At x=4, A=2, B=6; recall at x=6: B=6. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

recall.question: Six tickets expire at the event’s end. Six others remain valid later. Use four before the deadline. Change only Used to 6. What is B (Other-first) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Used=6: it gives 6tickets. Using deadline tickets first reduces the expiring remainder. Using the other tickets leaves all six deadline tickets unused. This is a declared ticket-validity model, not guidance about food or unsafe expired goods.

safety.assumptions: Six tickets expire at the event’s end. Six others remain valid later. Use four before the deadline.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
